## Recap of Friday

| Verb | Job |
|------|-----|
| `select()` | Keep columns |
| `filter()` | Keep rows that match a condition |
| `count()` | Count rows |
| `n()` | Count rows inside `summarize()` |
| `arrange()` | Sort rows |

The pipe `|>` connects them. Today we add three tools for `select()` and `filter()`.

---

## Our data: all flights from New York in 2013

```{r}
# Load the file once. Every chunk after this one starts from flights
flights <- read_csv(here("data", "flights.csv"))
```

```{r}
flights |>
  glimpse()
```

Examples from *R for Data Science* (2e), chapter 3.

---

# 1. Select a range {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Neighbouring columns**

---

## select(): typing every name is long

```{r}
# Seven names for a block of neighbouring columns
flights |>
  select(year, month, day, dep_time, sched_dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time)
```

---

## A range with a colon

```{r}
# year:day means every column from year to day
flights |>
  select(year:day)
```

---

## All columns except a range

```{r}
# ! means not: every column except year to day
flights |>
  select(!year:day)
```

The result has 16 columns, the 19 of `flights` minus 3.

---

# 2. Select by pattern {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Columns that share a start or an end**

---

## select(): columns that share a start

```{r}
# Two columns begin with dep. Typing both names is easy,
# but a table with 50 such columns is not.
flights |>
  select(dep_time, dep_delay)
```

---

## starts_with() picks columns by their first letters

```{r}
# starts_with("abc") keeps every column whose name begins with abc
flights |>
  select(starts_with("dep"))
```

The result has 2 columns: `dep_time` and `dep_delay`.

---

## ends_with() picks columns by their last letters

```{r}
# ends_with("xyz") keeps every column whose name ends with xyz
flights |>
  select(ends_with("delay"))
```

The result has 2 columns: `dep_delay` and `arr_delay`.

---


Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] columns.

```{r}

  select(starts_with("___"))
```

Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] columns.

# 3. AND and OR {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**More than one condition in `filter()`**

---

## filter(): AND

```{r}
# & means and: both conditions must be TRUE
# Flights that departed on January 1
flights |>
  filter(month == 1 & day == 1)
```

A comma gives the same result: `filter(month == 1, day == 1)`.

---

## Flights in January or February?

```{r}
# A flight has one month, so no row can be January and February
flights |>
  filter(month == 1 & month == 2)
```

The result has 0 rows.

---

## filter(): OR

```{r}
# | means or: one condition is enough
# Flights that departed in January or February
flights |>
  filter(month == 1 | month == 2)
```

---

## A shortcut: %in%

```{r}
# %in% checks if the value is one of the values in c()
flights |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 2))
```

The result is the same as the previous slide.

---

## A common mistake with OR

```{r}
# Written as in English: "month is 1 or 2"
flights |>
  filter(month == 1 | 2) |>
  count(month)
```

R runs this without an error. `|` checks `month == 1`, then checks `2`, and `2` counts as TRUE for every row. The table shows all 12 months.

---

## The fix

```{r}
# Repeat the full condition, or use %in%
flights |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 2)) |>
  count(month)
```

---

# 4. NOT {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**Reverse a condition**

---

## Every month except January and February

```{r}
# Works, but we repeat the column name and use two conditions
flights |>
  filter(month != 1 & month != 2)
```

---

## ! reverses a condition

```{r}
# month %in% c(1, 2) is TRUE for January and February
# ! turns TRUE into FALSE and FALSE into TRUE
flights |>
  filter(!(month %in% c(1, 2)))
```

The result is the same as the previous slide, with one condition.

---

## Finding missing values

```{r}
# NA means "unknown", so a comparison with NA is never TRUE
flights |>
  filter(dep_delay == NA)
```

The result has 0 rows.

```{r}
# is.na() is TRUE when the value is missing
flights |>
  filter(is.na(dep_delay))
```

---

## Keep the rows that have a value

```{r}
# ! reverses is.na(): keep flights with a departure delay
flights |>
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay))
```

---

**Flights that did not depart from JFK or LGA.**

```{r}
#| eval: false
flights |>
  filter(!(origin %in% c("___", "___"))) |>

```

Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] is the only airport left.

---

## Recap {.smaller}

| Task | Code |
|------|------|
| A range of columns | `select(year:day)` |
| All columns except a range | `select(!year:day)` |
| Columns by pattern | `select(starts_with("dep"))`, `select(ends_with("delay"))` |
| AND | `filter(month == 1 & day == 1)` |
| OR | `filter(month == 1 \| month == 2)`, or `month %in% c(1, 2)` |
| NOT | `filter(!(month %in% c(1, 2)))` |
| Missing values | `filter(is.na(dep_delay))`, `filter(!is.na(dep_delay))` |
